title: Insurance claim and superbill generation
problem: Acupuncturists spend significant time manually filling out CMS-1500 forms and superbills for each patient visit. Incorrect codes or missing information leads to claim denials and delayed reimbursement. Solo practitioners without billing staff lose hours weekly on paperwork instead of treating patients.
who: Solo and small-practice acupuncturists accepting insurance

skill_spec.name: Acupuncture Superbill & CMS-1500 Generator
skill_spec.one_liner: Generates completed superbills and CMS-1500 claim forms from visit details with correct CPT and ICD-10 codes
skill_spec.structure_hint: Patient demographics -> ICD-10 codes (mapped from diagnosis) -> CPT codes (97810, 97811, 97813, 97814 for acupuncture) -> units based on duration -> provider info -> fee schedule -> total charges

example_queries: Generate a superbill for a patient with low back pain, 30-minute acupuncture session with 12 needles and cupping
Fill out a CMS-1500 for initial acupuncture evaluation with e-stim, ICD-10 M54.5

title: Practice revenue and session pricing calculator
problem: Acupuncturists struggle to price their services profitably, especially when balancing insurance reimbursements with self-pay rates. Many undercharge because they don't account for overhead, taxes, and self-employment costs. Financial instability is the top fear in the profession.
who: Solo practice owners and new graduates starting practices

skill_spec.name: Acupuncture Session Pricing Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates optimal session pricing based on overhead, target income, patient volume, and tax obligations

outputs.name: minimum_session_rate
outputs.label: Minimum session rate to break even (USD)

skill_spec.formula_hint: annual_overhead = (rent + supplies + insurance + other) * 12; SE_tax = gross * 0.9235 * 0.153; federal_tax = bracket-based; gross_needed = (target_income + annual_overhead + SE_tax + federal_tax) / (1 - state_tax_rate); min_rate = gross_needed / (patients_per_week * weeks_worked)

example_queries: I want to take home $80,000/year seeing 20 patients a week. My rent is $1,500/month. What should I charge per session?
Calculate my minimum session rate with $3,000 monthly overhead and 25 patients per week in California

title: Self-employment quarterly tax estimation
problem: Most acupuncturists are self-employed and must calculate and pay quarterly estimated taxes to the IRS. Many miscalculate, leading to underpayment penalties or cash flow problems. They juggle federal income tax, self-employment tax, and state taxes without dedicated accounting support.
who: Self-employed solo practitioners and practice owners

skill_spec.name: Acupuncturist Quarterly Tax Estimator
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates quarterly estimated tax payments for self-employed acupuncturists including SE tax, federal income tax, and state tax
skill_spec.formula_hint: net_income = gross - expenses; SE_tax = net_income * 0.9235 * 0.153; SE_deduction = SE_tax / 2; AGI = net_income - SE_deduction + other_income; federal_tax = bracket_based(AGI, filing_status); quarterly = (federal_tax + SE_tax + state_tax) / 4

example_queries: I made $22,000 this quarter with $5,000 in expenses, single filer in New York. What's my quarterly estimated tax?
Calculate my 1040-ES payment - $90,000 annual practice income, $20,000 expenses, married filing jointly in Oregon

title: NCCAOM recertification PDA tracking
problem: Acupuncturists must earn 60 PDA points over 4 years for NCCAOM recertification, spread across specific categories (safety, ethics, core competencies). Tracking which categories are fulfilled and what's still needed is confusing. Missing the deadline means loss of certification and potentially licensure.

skill_spec.name: NCCAOM PDA Points Tracker & Calculator
skill_spec.one_liner: Tracks PDA points earned across categories and calculates remaining requirements for NCCAOM recertification

outputs.name: monthly_pace_needed
outputs.label: PDA points needed per month to stay on track

skill_spec.formula_hint: total_required = 60; safety_min = 4 (CNT); ethics_min = 2; core_min = 30; remaining = 60 - total_completed; monthly_pace = remaining / months_left; check each category minimum separately

example_queries: I have 35 PDA points with 18 months left in my cycle. Am I on track? I have 4 safety, 1 ethics, 20 core
How many PDA points per month do I need if my recertification is due in March 2027 and I have 22 points?

title: State licensure requirements lookup
problem: Acupuncture licensing varies dramatically across 47 states - different titles (LAc, AP, CA), different CE requirements, different scope of practice (herbs, dry needling, injection therapy). Practitioners relocating or maintaining multi-state licenses waste hours researching each state's specific rules.
who: Acupuncturists relocating, adding state licenses, or new graduates choosing where to practice

skill_spec.name: State Acupuncture Licensure Reference
skill_spec.one_liner: Quick lookup of state-specific acupuncture licensure requirements, titles, scope, and renewal rules
skill_spec.data_domain: State acupuncture practice acts, licensing requirements, and scope of practice across all US states

key_sections: Scope of practice (herbs, dry needling, injection)

example_queries: What are the licensure requirements for acupuncture in Texas? Do they require NCCAOM?
Which states allow acupuncturists to prescribe herbal medicine?
I'm licensed in California - what do I need to also practice in New York?

title: SOAP notes and treatment plan documentation
problem: Acupuncturists must document every visit with detailed SOAP notes including TCM diagnoses, point selection rationale, and treatment outcomes. Insurance requires Western diagnosis codes alongside TCM patterns. Writing thorough notes for 15-30 patients weekly is exhausting and cuts into clinical time.
who: All practicing acupuncturists, especially those accepting insurance

skill_spec.name: Acupuncture SOAP Note Generator
skill_spec.one_liner: Generates professional SOAP notes with TCM and Western diagnoses, point prescriptions, and treatment rationale

variables.name: subjective
variables.label: Patient-reported symptoms and changes since last visit

variables.name: additional_modalities
variables.label: Additional modalities (cupping, moxa, e-stim, tui na)

skill_spec.structure_hint: S: Subjective (symptoms, changes) -> O: Objective (tongue, pulse, palpation, vitals) -> A: Assessment (TCM pattern + ICD-10) -> P: Plan (points rationale, modalities, frequency, home care recommendations)

example_queries: Write a SOAP note for a migraine patient - Liver Yang Rising, tongue red with thin yellow coating, wiry pulse, used LV3, LI4, GB20, GB41, Taiyang
Generate progress notes for visit 5 of a low back pain patient showing 60% improvement with Kidney Qi deficiency pattern

title: Insurance claim denial appeal
problem: Insurance claim denials are a top frustration for acupuncturists. Common denial reasons include medical necessity, incorrect coding, exceeded visit limits, or missing prior authorization. Writing effective appeal letters requires knowledge of payer-specific rules and clinical documentation standards.
who: Acupuncturists billing insurance, especially those without billing staff

skill_spec.name: Insurance Denial Appeal Letter Generator
skill_spec.one_liner: Generates professional appeal letters for denied acupuncture insurance claims with clinical justification

variables.name: denial_reason
variables.label: Denial reason (medical necessity, coding, visit limit, etc.)

skill_spec.structure_hint: Formal header -> Claim identification -> Denial reason acknowledgment -> Clinical justification with evidence -> Reference to payer's own coverage policy -> Treatment necessity argument citing outcomes -> Research citations if applicable -> Request for reconsideration -> Provider signature

example_queries: Write an appeal letter for a denied claim - Aetna says acupuncture for chronic low back pain is not medically necessary after 12 visits
Help me appeal a Blue Cross denial for acupuncture migraine treatment, claim number BC-2026-445521

title: CPT and ICD-10 coding for acupuncture
problem: Acupuncturists frequently struggle with correct CPT and ICD-10 code selection. Using wrong codes causes claim denials and potential audit flags. Mapping TCM diagnoses to ICD-10 codes is not intuitive, and acupuncture-specific CPT codes (97810-97814) have specific time and needle requirements.
who: All acupuncturists billing insurance or creating superbills

skill_spec.name: Acupuncture CPT & ICD-10 Code Reference
skill_spec.one_liner: Quick lookup of correct CPT codes for acupuncture procedures and ICD-10 mappings from TCM diagnoses
skill_spec.data_domain: Acupuncture CPT procedure codes, ICD-10 diagnosis codes, and TCM-to-ICD-10 mapping

data_hints.source_law: AMA CPT Code Manual, WHO ICD-10-CM

example_queries: What CPT code do I use for a 45-minute acupuncture session with electroacupuncture?
What ICD-10 code maps to Liver Qi Stagnation with headache?
Can I bill 97810 and 97140 together for acupuncture plus tui na?

title: Informed consent form generation
problem: Acupuncturists need comprehensive informed consent forms covering needle risks (pneumothorax, nerve damage, bruising), herbal medicine interactions, and state-specific disclosure requirements. Generic templates may not cover state-mandated disclosures, creating legal liability.
who: All practicing acupuncturists, especially new practitioners setting up their practice

skill_spec.name: Acupuncture Informed Consent Generator
skill_spec.one_liner: Generates state-compliant informed consent forms for acupuncture, herbal medicine, and adjunctive therapies

variables.name: modalities
variables.label: Modalities offered (acupuncture, herbs, cupping, moxa, e-stim, tui na)

skill_spec.structure_hint: Practice identification -> Description of acupuncture and TCM -> Procedures offered -> Potential risks and side effects (bruising, fainting, pneumothorax, nerve injury, infection) -> Herbal medicine risks (if applicable) -> Alternative treatments available -> Right to refuse -> HIPAA notice -> State-specific disclosures -> Patient acknowledgment and signature -> Date

example_queries: Generate an informed consent form for my acupuncture practice in Florida that includes herbs and cupping
Create a consent form for a California LAc offering acupuncture, moxa, and e-stim - what state-specific disclosures do I need?

title: Herbal formula interaction and safety check
problem: Acupuncturists prescribing Chinese herbal formulas must check for drug-herb interactions, contraindications, and pregnancy safety. With patients on multiple Western medications, the risk of adverse interactions is significant. Manual cross-referencing across pharmacopeias is time-consuming and error-prone.
who: Acupuncturists with herbal prescribing privileges (Dipl.CH, states allowing herbs)

skill_spec.name: Chinese Herbal Formula Safety Advisor
skill_spec.one_liner: Checks Chinese herbal formulas for drug-herb interactions, contraindications, pregnancy safety, and dosage guidance
skill_spec.expertise_area: Chinese herbal medicine pharmacology, drug-herb interactions, and safety

example_queries: Is it safe to prescribe Xiao Yao San for a patient taking warfarin and metformin?
Check interactions for Bu Zhong Yi Qi Tang with lisinopril and atorvastatin
Which herbs in Gui Pi Tang are contraindicated during pregnancy?

title: New practice setup checklist
problem: Opening an acupuncture practice involves dozens of steps across licensing, business formation, insurance credentialing, HIPAA compliance, and space setup. New graduates often miss critical steps like NPI registration, CLIA waiver, or proper waste disposal contracts. Mistakes cause costly delays.
who: New graduates and acupuncturists transitioning to solo practice

skill_spec.name: Acupuncture Practice Setup Checklist
skill_spec.one_liner: Complete step-by-step checklist for opening an acupuncture practice from licensing through first patient
steps: Step 1: Verify state license is active and in good standing
Step 2: Register business entity (LLC, PLLC, or S-Corp) with state
Step 3: Get EIN from IRS (Form SS-4)
Step 4: Apply for NPI number (Type 1 individual provider)
Step 5: Open business bank account
Step 6: Obtain malpractice insurance (ASCA, CM&F, or state-specific)
Step 7: Get general liability and property insurance
Step 8: Secure office space with proper zoning for healthcare
Step 9: Set up sharps disposal and biohazard waste contract
Step 10: Implement HIPAA compliance (privacy policy, BAAs, secure records)
Step 11: Credential with insurance panels (Aetna, BCBS, Cigna, UHC, etc.)
Step 12: Enroll as Medicare provider (if accepting Medicare)
Step 13: Set up EHR/practice management software
Step 14: Create intake forms, consent forms, and HIPAA notice of privacy
Step 15: Establish fee schedule and sliding scale policy
Step 16: Order supplies (needles, moxa, cups, herbs, linens)
Step 17: Set up online scheduling and payment processing
Step 18: Register with state sales tax (if selling herbs/products)
Step 19: Create Google Business profile and directory listings
Step 20: Set up quarterly estimated tax payments (IRS Form 1040-ES)
warnings: Warning: Insurance credentialing can take 90-180 days - start early
Warning: HIPAA violations can result in fines from $100 to $50,000 per violation
Warning: Sharps disposal without proper contract may violate OSHA regulations
Warning: Some states require separate herb dispensing license

example_queries: I just passed my NCCAOM exams and want to open a practice in Colorado. What do I need to do?
What's the complete checklist for setting up an acupuncture clinic? I don't want to miss anything

title: Insurance reimbursement rate comparison
problem: Acupuncturists negotiate with multiple insurance companies but lack visibility into typical reimbursement rates for their CPT codes. They often accept unfavorable contracts because they don't know what others are getting. Comparing rates across payers is critical for deciding which panels to join.
who: Acupuncturists credentialing with insurance companies or renegotiating contracts

skill_spec.name: Acupuncture Reimbursement Rate Analyzer
skill_spec.one_liner: Calculates and compares insurance reimbursement rates per visit against your costs to determine panel profitability

inputs.name: avg_units_per_visit
inputs.label: Average number of units billed per visit

inputs.name: cost_per_hour
inputs.label: Your cost per clinical hour (overhead + target income)

skill_spec.formula_hint: revenue_per_visit = initial_code_rate + (additional_units * reinsertion_rate); cost_per_visit = cost_per_hour * (visit_duration / 60); profit = revenue - cost; effective_hourly = revenue / (visit_duration / 60); recommend if effective_hourly > cost_per_hour * 1.3

example_queries: Aetna offers $45 for 97810 and $32 for 97811. My overhead is $85/hour. Is this panel worth joining?
Compare my BCBS rates to Medicare rates for acupuncture codes - am I getting a fair deal?

title: Adverse event response procedure
problem: When a patient experiences an adverse event (stuck needle, pneumothorax, severe bruising, fainting, allergic reaction to herbs), acupuncturists must follow specific clinical and legal protocols. Panic in the moment leads to documentation failures that increase malpractice exposure.

skill_spec.name: Acupuncture Adverse Event Response Protocol
skill_spec.one_liner: Step-by-step emergency response protocol for adverse events during acupuncture treatment
steps: Step 1: STOP treatment immediately - remove all needles if safe to do so
Step 2: Assess patient condition (consciousness, breathing, vital signs)
Step 3: Call 911 if life-threatening (suspected pneumothorax, cardiac event, severe allergic reaction)
Step 4: Administer first aid as appropriate (pressure for bleeding, position for fainting)
Step 5: Stay with patient - do NOT leave them unattended
Step 6: Document everything in real-time with timestamps
Step 7: Notify patient's emergency contact if condition is serious
Step 8: Complete incident report form within 24 hours
Step 9: Notify malpractice insurance carrier within required timeframe
Step 10: Do NOT admit fault or make statements about causation
Step 11: Preserve all treatment records and needle packaging/lot numbers
Step 12: Report to state board if required by state law
Step 13: Schedule follow-up with patient within 24-48 hours
Step 14: Review and update safety protocols based on incident
warnings: Warning: Suspected pneumothorax (sudden chest pain, difficulty breathing) - CALL 911 IMMEDIATELY
Warning: Never destroy or alter records after an adverse event
Warning: Contact your malpractice insurer BEFORE discussing the incident with the patient's attorney
Warning: Some states mandate reporting adverse events to the state board within specific timeframes
regulatory_refs: State Acupuncture Practice Act adverse event reporting

example_queries: A patient is complaining of sharp chest pain after needling near the upper back - what do I do?
My patient fainted during treatment and hit their head. Walk me through the proper protocol
